title: CareBridge POC: deployment options quickscan
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a rapid-options brief to support the CareBridge POC kick-off (internal demo + 3-week pilot). Aim: give the customer a concise comparison of hosting modes (hosted, dedicated, private) and a concrete hybrid recommendation that balances their two hard constraints: sub-200ms median inference latency for chat UX and strict EHR PHI residency in EU region.

Quick summary recommendation (first draft):
- Short term (pilot): Use Redwood Hosted with EU-only tenancy + in-transit protections, combined with per-request data masking for PHI-sensitive fields. This minimizes onboarding friction and allows us to validate UX under real traffic while keeping costs modest.
- Mid term (production if successful): Move to a Dedicated pool in an EU region with customer-managed VPC peering and encrypted-at-rest keys in their KMS. This meets residency and SLA needs while keeping Redwood-managed runtime and autoscaling.
- Long term (if regulatory audit/air-gap required): Private deployment (on-prem or VPC-hosted private control plane) as a contract add-on; plan for a phased move with data migration and acceptance testing.

Driver checklist (customer constraints):
- Latency target: median <= 200ms, p95 <= 700ms for 1–2k concurrent sessions.
- Data residency: all patient-identifying data must remain in EU tenancy; logs retention policy must be configurable by the customer.
- Audit/compliance: support for customer KMS, access logs export, and SOC2 review evidence.
- Integration: connectors to CareBridge EHR (HL7 FHIR) over a private link preferred.

Option analysis (short bullets):
1) Hosted (Redwood API, EU region)
   - Pros: fastest to start, minimal ops, immediate telemetry via Console, streaming supported. Good for validating model prompts, UX, and routing policies.
   - Cons: may not satisfy strict legal teams without explicit private control plane; logs and raw payloads flow through Redwood-managed infra (we can scope and minimize via retention controls but not fully hand off).
   - Risk mitigations: EU-only tenancy, strict log redaction rules, contract addendum for limited retention, endpoint-level masking hooks.
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in EU)
   - Pros: predictable throughput, isolated capacity, integration with customer VPC peering and KMS. Strong fit for production at scale and predictable budgets.
   - Cons: longer lead time (2–4 weeks to provision), requires traffic shaping changes and network setup.
   - Notes: we can stage via a small reserved instance and enable autoscale policies for burst traffic.
3) Private (VPC/private control plane / on-prem)
   - Pros: maximum isolation, best for regulated customers requiring full control.
   - Cons: highest ops and testing effort; more expensive; lifecycle (patches, upgrades) requires coordination.
   - Consideration: if they require offline air-gapped model validation or vendor-managed image delivery, add 6–8 week plan.

Hybrid variations worth considering:
- Host-to-dedicated bridge: start on hosted for pilot, then lift-and-shift to dedicated with identical model/artifact versions and canary routing. This minimizes customer-visible changes.
- Private control plane + Redwood-managed runtime in customer VPC: lowers on-prem footprint while satisfying control plane needs.
- Edge cache for prompt prefixes: place small edge caching layer (regionally located) to cache warm KV prefixes and reduce token cost and p95 latency spikes.

Performance/back-of-envelope cost tradeoffs (pilot estimates):
- Hosted pilot (EU-small usage): ~50k tokens/day -> cost X (approx €1.4k/mo) + estimated infra overhead for streaming.
- Dedicated small pool (1x A10G-equivalent reserved): upfront commit ~€12k/mo, amortized if we expect sustained >200k tokens/day.
- Private: one-time onboarding (professional services estimate €30–50k) + infra recurring similar to dedicated depending on GPU selection.
- Note: exact numbers to be updated by FinOps; these are initial order-of-magnitude figures to help choose path.

Deployment topology (sketch):
- Pilot topology (hosted): CareBridge webapp -> private LB -> Redwood EU-hosted API (restricted keys) -> model runtime (Llama-variant)
  - Add per-request middleware to strip/replace PHI fields before logging.
  - Monitoring: instrument token-level traces and per-route latency SLOs in Redwood Console.
- Production topology (dedicated): CareBridge VPC peering -> Redwood Dedicated pool (EU) -> KMS-managed key for model artifacts and logs -> optional on‑prem FHIR connector via VPN.
- Optional: local inference proxy that only sends non-PHI context (or tokenized context) to Redwood to reduce regulatory surface.

Implementation checklist (pilot, 3-week sprint):
- Week 0: confirm legal scoping + sign pilot DPA addendum (owner: Legal, referenced: CONF-1427).
- Week 0–1: crate test harness & sample prompt set derived from CareBridge T&Cs; run synthetic latency load. (owner: SE + Applied ML)
- Week 1: enable EU tenancy, create masked logging pipeline, validate KMS access pattern in a sandbox. (owner: Infra)
- Week 2: integrate EHR connector stub, run end-to-end demo with product team, measure p50/p95, and collect quality signals. (owner: Solutions)
- Week 3: review results, present go/no-go to carebridge stakeholders with proposed date for dedicated provisioning if metrics meet thresholds. (owner: Customer Success)

Operational playbook notes (practical tips):
- Use prefix caching for common system prompts to reduce per-chat tokenization cost. Document which fields are safe to cache.
- For latency-sensitive paths, prefer smaller context windows and retrieve additional patient data lazily.
- Turn on detailed traces only during test windows; redact user PHI in traces.

Open questions / items for customer clarifications:
- Can CareBridge accept partial redaction (hashing IDs) prior to sending PII? If not, private deployment required.
- Expected sustained traffic after pilot (we used 2k concurrent sessions as target; confirm).
- Does CareBridge require on-prem artifact signing or only KMS-based key control?

Risks and mitigations (short):
- Risk: legal pushes back on hosted logs. Mitigation: offer a short-term DPA clause + immediate log retention reduction + audit export to customer bucket.
- Risk: p95 volatility due to cold KV cache. Mitigation: pre-warm KV caches at rollout, use canary ramping.

Next steps before customer meeting:
- Prepare three visual diagrams (hosted, dedicated, private) with clear ownership arrows (infra vs customer) (owner: Design).
- Attach sample masked transcript examples and prompt set used for QoE evaluation (owner: Applied ML).
- Get Budget estimate from FinOps for 3-month hosted pilot vs 6-month dedicated commit. (owner: Finance)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- If CareBridge mentions vendor lock concerns, emphasize model portability and identical API semantics across deployment modes.
- Consider offering a temporary logging-forwarder that streams redacted logs into customer's EU S3 bucket (small engineering spike).

Slack refs and related tickets:
- convo: #carebridge-onboarding (link pinned with demo recordings)
- ticket: JIRA-SVC-3892 (customer connector and network setup)

Appendix: short decision rubric we will use in the go/no-go: 
- UX: p50 < 200ms and p95 < 700ms under pilot traffic -> pass
- Security: DPA + KMS access or acceptable redaction strategy -> pass
- Cost: delta between hosted and dedicated < 20% over 6 months (given forecast) -> prefer dedicated

End of quickscan. Intend to tidy this into a customer-facing one-pager after the kick-off call.
